### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 |
| **Summary** | This is the general Springer Nature publisher policy (link.springer.com pages for this specific journal returned login-walled redirects, so a journal-specific AI policy page could not be directly confirmed — treat as publisher default applied to this journal). Facts per Springer's public AI policy: (1) LLMs/generative AI tools cannot be listed as authors — authorship requires accountability an AI cannot bear. (2) Any use of an LLM in preparing the manuscript must be disclosed (documented in the Methods section, or a suitable alternative section if no Methods section exists, per general Springer text; a related Springer Nature journal update page phrases it as 'declared in the Introduction or Acknowledgements'). (3) AI-assisted copyediting for grammar/style/readability does NOT need to be declared. (4) AI-generated images cannot be included in publications. (5) Peer reviewers must transparently declare in their review report if they used an AI tool to help evaluate the manuscript. (6) Springer states a 'zero tolerance' stance on deliberate, non-transparent misuse of generative AI. Leniency scored 3 (moderate/conditional) because AI assistance is permitted with mandatory disclosure, not banned outright, but authorship and undisclosed use are hard-blocked -- hence gate = conditional (disclosure required, not a blanket ban or blanket allowance). |
| **Source URL** | https://www.springer.com/gp/editorial-policies/artificial-intelligence--ai-/25428500 (publisher-level Springer Nature policy; no Psychological-Record-specific AI policy page was independently accessible) |

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** The journal (published by Springer in partnership with the Association for Behavior Analysis International, ABAI) is explicitly scoped to behavior analysis, behavior science, and behavior theory: basic behavioral-process research, translational studies bridging experimental and applied behavior analysis, and conceptual/philosophy-of-behaviorism pieces. A January 2025 editorial by the new editorial leadership, 'A Global Vision for The Psychological Record: Innovation, Inclusivity, and Impact,' signals an explicit push toward international/inclusive submissions and continued coverage across basic, applied, translational, and conceptual behavior-analytic research (full text of this editorial could not be fetched directly — link.springer.com article pages redirected to a login wall — so this is based on the article title plus search-engine summary snippets, not a direct read).

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** single-case/within-subject experimental designs (behavior-analytic tradition), basic behavioral-process (laboratory) studies, translational research bridging basic and applied behavior analysis, applied behavior analysis studies, conceptual/theoretical and philosophy-of-behaviorism papers
